merge_request.title: Draw the induced current on the ACID isosurface

notes.body:
## Codex automated review

Reviewed commit `8115ca60652c` with the official Codex CLI.

Current vectors can diverge from the displayed isosurface threshold, and log restoration loses or incorrectly retains the new field state. These affect the correctness of the scientific visualization.

Full review comments:

- [P2] Match the vector mask to the rendered surface threshold — /var/lib/codex-review/work/project-18-mr-1/frontend/public/viewer/app.js:2478-2483
  When the Surface size control differs from 100%, the arrows are sampled against a different threshold from the visible surface. `setVolume()` divides the isovalue by `surfaceSize` and applies a `maxAbs * 0.0025` minimum, whereas this calculation does neither. For example, at 10% surface size the rendered threshold is ten times the arrow threshold, entirely outside the selected three-times-threshold band. Use the same effective isolation calculation for both so the vectors remain on the displayed ACID shell.

- [P2] Include current-density state in log snapshot restoration — /var/lib/codex-review/work/project-18-mr-1/frontend/public/viewer/app.js:2531-2533
  Loading an ACID set, loading another molecule, and then clicking the ACID log entry restores only its scalar surface: `createLogSnapshot()` and `restoreLogSnapshot()` never save or restore `currentField`. Conversely, restoring an older scalar cube with the same grid can retain the newer molecule's current vectors because the grid check passes. Include the field and its controls in snapshot capture/restoration, explicitly clearing it for snapshots without current data.

<!-- codex-review-runner sha:8115ca60652ca92632a714bb90614921b861ac17 -->
